_comment: The pre-built decks whose printed contents a pack's collector-number run cannot
give on its own. build_decks reads every other deck straight out of marvelsdb: a
hero pack lists its cards in printed order, so the run from one identity to the
next is that identity's precon. 58 of the 67 come to exactly 40 cards that way,
and 24 of the finished decks were checked card for card against marvelcdb's
published precon lists -- every one agreed.
Keyed on the identity's code. A set name can change upstream; a code does not. A
key no deck is built for fails the build rather than sitting here doing nothing.
'aspect'    build the Core Set's shared aspect pool for this aspect into the deck.
'slots'     override the printed quantity of a card in the run, or add one to it.
'exclude'   drop a card the run holds but the deck does not.
'set_aside' move a card out of the deck and in beside it, keeping its quantity.
Every entry says why. A precon is a physical fact about a box, so the reason has
to be checkable against something -- the save, the card's own text, or a printed
list -- and not a guess that happens to reach 40.

_core: The Core Set's five. Core prints ONE shared aspect pool at positions 50-93 for
all five heroes, so a hero's run stops at its 15 signature cards and the other
25 are a pool nothing in the data assigns to anyone. The aspect below is from
marvelcdb's precon lists; the cards follow from it by the rule the box uses --
one copy of each unique card in that aspect's block, two of each non-unique, and
one of each of the eleven basic cards. That reproduces marvelcdb's Spider-Man,
She-Hulk and Black Panther precons exactly, which is why this is a rule and not
_set_aside: Cards the run holds that do not go into the deck, and that marvelsdb does not
mark `permanent` for us to notice. The Tabletop Simulator save is the check: it
cannot give a deck list, but it does say what starts beside the deck rather than
in it, and it holds each of these loose in the pack bag or in a deck of its own.

38001a._why: Touched starts attached to an enemy, not in the deck. Loose in the save's Rogue Hero Pack bag beside her identity.

25001a._why: Death-Glow is attached to an enemy at setup. Loose in the save's Valkyrie Hero Pack bag.

50034a._why: Nick Fury's run is 39 because Assault and Stealth -- 50035a/b, the two sides of one card -- are set aside, which the save confirms by holding Assault loose in his pack bag. The run's own remainder is 39 and the box prints a fourth Covert Surveillance to make 40.

_team_up: A Team-Up card says 'Max 1 per deck' in its own text and carries deck_limit 1,
and a box prints two copies when both named partners are in it -- one for each
player -- and one copy when the partner ships elsewhere. build_decks caps every
card at its deck limit for this reason, which is what takes the nine packs that
print a doubled team-up down from 41 (Winter Soldier, with two, from 42) to 40.
Nebula is the one pack the other way about. Her run holds 39 once Daughters of
Thanos is capped, and her box has no fortieth card to reach for, so the second
copy is it -- the cap is lifted rather than a card invented. Worth revisiting if
her printed list ever turns up.

22001a._why: Nebula's run is 39 once Daughters of Thanos is capped, and her box holds no other card. The second copy is the fortieth.
